resources.string:
SleepAnalysis is a personal wellness and research tool — not a medical device.

 It does not diagnose, treat, or prevent any disease, including sleep apnea. It estimates simple measures like snoring from microphone sound; these estimates can be wrong and are not a substitute for a sleep study (polysomnography) or advice from a qualified clinician.

 If you regularly experience loud snoring, witnessed breathing pauses, gasping during sleep, or excessive daytime sleepiness, speak to a doctor.

• Microphone audio is processed on this device only — nothing is uploaded.

 • Full-night audio is never saved. Short clips (a few seconds) are kept for detected events so you can verify them, and are deleted automatically after your retention period.

 • All data stays in this app's private storage. You can delete a single night or everything at any time.
Put the phone on your nightstand, roughly 0.5–1 m from your head, with the microphone unobstructed. Keep it plugged in. Results vary with distance and background noise.
The microphone is used only while a recording session is running, and the ongoing notification shows you when it is active.

This removes every recording, event, clip, measurement and factor log entry. This cannot be undone.

Shown while overnight audio monitoring is active

Audio capture begins at %1$s — time to fall asleep. Tap Stop to cancel.

Master switch — when off, the app will not start a recording, schedule included.
Off by default — manual start stays the primary method.
Start and end time must differ.
Scheduling is off — recording starts manually.
Exact alarms are not permitted — the inexact fallback can be delayed by Doze, sometimes well beyond its ~10-minute window.
Notifications are turned off — the bedtime notification that starts a scheduled recording cannot be shown, so scheduled starts will not appear.
Timing uses exact system alarms (not WorkManager) for a precise bedtime; without exact-alarm permission it falls back to an inexact window that Doze can stretch beyond ~10 minutes on some devices.
Aggressive OEM battery managers can kill scheduled alarms — exclude SleepAnalysis from battery optimization.
Audio capture begins this many minutes after you tap start — time to fall asleep first. Time in bed still counts from the tap.

Your key is stored encrypted with the Android Keystore and never leaves this device except in requests to Garmin\'s API (personal.connectapi.garmin.com). Imports run only when you tap Import. No other network access exists in this app.

What was this? Tap to label (tap again to clear) — builds your personal dataset for better detection.

e.g. woke at 3am, phone on nightstand, partner snoring
You logged these for the day of this recording. User-entered context, not measurements.
No completed nights yet — insights appear once recordings are finalized.
Your recordings suggest nothing yet: no night passed the quality gate (validity grade A or B, same detector and score versions). Insights appear as eligible nights accumulate.
Collecting your baseline: %1$d eligible night(s) — 10 needed before patterns are worth showing.
Median and usual range over your last %1$d eligible nights. Bands are personal, not clinical ranges.
Regularity index %1$.0f — how steady your sleep timing is night to night (approximated from nightly Garmin windows; wrist-derived).
Social jetlag ≈ %1$.1f h between weekend and weekday midpoints (approximate — we don\'t know your work schedule).
Needs at least 5 nights with Garmin windows to estimate regularity.

Your recordings suggest your bedtime timing has been more scattered than usual lately. For context from large studies: ~1 h night-to-night variation looks stable, ~3 h looks erratic — this is a description, not a threshold and not advice.

Your recordings suggest your sleep regularity has been lower than your recent norm. Research links steadier timing with feeling more rested; whether making it steadier improves anything for you is not established.

Your weekend nights are ending more than an hour later than your weekday nights — a \"social jetlag\" flag from observational research. Approximate by convention: the app doesn\'t know your work schedule.

On this alcohol-logged night, snoring concentrated in the second half. Alcohol research describes this pattern — deeper sleep early, more disturbed sleep later. Your recordings suggest; they don\'t diagnose.

Snoring concentrated in the second half of this night. This can be entirely normal: late-night REM sleep brings irregular breathing and awakenings, and an untagged late-night wake does not mean something is wrong.
%1$s was outside your usual range tonight. Your recordings suggest — a single night can always be chance, and the band is personal, not clinical.
On nights you logged alcohol, your recordings suggest more awake time than on nights without. No amount or cutoff makes this safe or unsafe — the comparison is descriptive.
On nights you logged caffeine after 14:00, your recordings suggest somewhat more awake time or shorter sleep than on other nights. Research reports small average effects; these numbers are yours.
On this exercise-logged night, awake time ran above your usual range. We can\'t tell when or how hard you exercised — the app records only the fact — so this is association, not a mechanism.

On nights you logged high stress, your wrist rMSSD ran lower and awake time higher than your usual range. Stress physiology and wrist sensors are both imperfect — your recordings suggest; they don\'t diagnose.
No clips to label for this session.
Every clip is labeled — thank you. Toggle "Hide labeled" off to review or change labels.
